# Publish gate report

**Going out:** Search ad (headline + description), UK audience, timing not specified.

## Checks

**Claims**
| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "The UK's number one tea subscription" | **Unproven.** Not on the policy list, no source given. It's a superlative/ranking claim. Remove. |
| "Subscribers can pause or cancel any time" | On policy list. OK. |
| "Free UK delivery on orders over £25" | On policy list. OK. |

**Regulated claims:** Touches prices/offers. The free delivery threshold matches the policy exactly and has no countdown or urgency. Fine. The only risk is the ranking claim, covered above.

**House style:** No policy voice section was provided beyond claims, so I checked for AI tells and banned patterns. Copy is plain. The "number one" line is the only weak spot, and it goes anyway.

**Disclosure:** A search ad is the brand's own paid ad, and the platform labels it as an ad (e.g. "Sponsored"/"Ad"). No creators, affiliates or AI imagery involved. Nothing to add.

## Fixed (suggested rewrite)
- Removed the "number one" ranking claim.

**Suggested copy:**
Headline: Tea Subscription UK
Description: Loose leaf and plastic-free tea, delivered monthly. Pause or cancel any time. Free UK delivery on orders over £25.

(Loose leaf and plastic-free bags are product facts, so they are fine as written.)

## Needs a decision
- If you really want a ranking claim, I need a current, like-for-like source (e.g. a named survey or market report) and it should be added to the policy. Until then, my suggestion is to drop it.
- Approver: the policy doesn't name one, so the approval must come from you. I haven't recorded any approval. Please confirm yes to the revised copy above (not the original), and it can go out.

**Status: not approved to publish as drafted.**
